    "rationale": "Critique points accepted: (1) kd=0.6 is mis-scaled. One 10 ms step adds 100*kd*(signal change) turn units, so kd=0.6 amplifies sensor noise. I return kd to 0.1, a value already tested, so its effect is not confounded. (2) The 5-sensor array at +/-0.03 m with 12 mm footprints and 15 mm spacing leaves a gap, and the normalised signal saturates at about +/-1 once only an outer sensor sees tape. I widen to 7 sensors at 15 mm spacing spanning +/-0.045 m, with 16 mm footprints so adjacent sensors overlap and no gap can exist. Weights are linear, -1.5 to +1.5, so a single outer sensor still gives a graded signal of about +/-1.5 rather than a flat +/-1. (3) Wheel saturation: at base_speed 1.5, base PWM is 3071 and headroom to 4095 is about 1024. With kp 2.0 and |signal| up to 1.5, turn is at most 3.0 units, about 1050 PWM, so saturation is only reached at the extreme of the array. kp is lowered from 4.0 to 2.0 so steering authority is not lost on sharp bends. (4) ki is set to 0.3, not 0. The integral is clamped to +/-2, so the maximum contribution is 0.6 turn units. The hypothesis is that the seeded left/right motor mismatch produces a steady offset that a proportional-only loop cannot remove. This is a hypothesis, not a result. Iteration 1 showed ki=0.0 and ki=0.05 gave the same failure, so ki is a test variable, not a claimed fix.\n\nWhat I rejected: I did not change mass or wheel_track. The critique is right that changing them with other variables prevents attribution. Geometry is kept at body 0.12 x 0.18 m, mass 0.8 kg, track 0.12 m, radius 0.03 m. I did not cut base_speed to 1.4 because completion (500 points) needs about 1.5 m/s average. I chose 1.5, a compromise that keeps the saturation headroom above.\n\nEvidence basis: all 60 development trials were off track with progress 0.06 to 0.17 and 2 line-loss events each. Iterations 0 and 1 changed sensor size, kp, kd, ki and speed, yet scores barely moved. So the failure is probably set early or by a structural cause (sensor coverage or steady bias), not by gain tuning. This design tests two structural changes at once: sensor span and integral action. If the result is poor, the cause cannot be fully attributed, and the next iteration should separate them.\n\nFalsifiable criteria for the next race: max_error below 0.06 m on the oval and s-bend; line_loss_events at most 1 per run; progress above 0.5 on all tracks. If max_error stays above 0.06 with no line losses, the cause is steady bias, and ki should rise. If line_loss_events stay at 2, the cause is sensor coverage, and the footprint or span should change. If steering_oscillation exceeds 0.18, kd or kp is too high. Reversal: if progress falls below the iteration-1 baseline of 0.17, revert kp to 4.0 and the 5-sensor array.",
